FAB approves proposed Dhs15b rights issue at Dhs13.52 per share
sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) announced that its Board of Directors has approved a proposal to raise up to Dhs15 billion through a strategic rights issue, subject to the required shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The proposed issue will provide additional capacity to support FAB’s next phase of growth in the UAE and across its international network, while maintaining the capital strength, liquidity and financial flexibility underpinning its medium-term ambitions.

Since 2020, FAB’s total assets have increased by more than 50 per cent to Dhs1.4 trillion, while net income has doubled to Dhs21.1 billion. Return on tangible equity (RoTE) has risen by 6.2 percentage points to 19.2 per cent.

Between 2020 and 2025, the bank distributed Dhs44 billion in cash dividends to shareholders, representing nearly 20 per cent of all cash dividends on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX), while maintaining its AA- credit strength.
Over the same period, FAB expanded its international presence, becoming the first bank from the Middle East and Africa to establish a global banking franchise.
The Group now operates across more than 20 markets, connecting clients through 25 UAE-linked trade corridors.

The proposed rights issue aims to strengthen FAB’s ability to capitalise on growth opportunities in the UAE and internationally, deepen client relationships and support continued investment in strategic capabilities, including technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

UAE's biggest bank FAB to raise $4.08bn to boost next phase of growth strategy
sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank plans to raise Dh15 billion ($4.08 billion) through a rights issue as it prepares for “the next phase” of its growth strategy across the UAE and its global portfolio.
The UAE's biggest bank will be offering 1,109,467,456 new shares, with each to be offered at Dh13.52, a 30 per cent discount on its closing share price on Tuesday, a FAB statement on Wednesday said.

“The UAE continues to advance an ambitious long-term economic agenda, underpinned by diversification, investment, innovation and a growing role in global trade and capital flows,” said Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, chairman of FAB.

“FAB is at the centre of this growth, enabling strategic investment across the UAE and internationally. The proposed rights issue will further strengthen FAB’s ability to support the UAE’s ambitions and capture the opportunities ahead.”
The rights issue is also meant to capture “significant opportunities” in the UAE and across FAB's international network, group chief executive Hana Al Rostamani said.
Aside from the Gulf, FAB also maintains a presence in the Middle East, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.
“The strength of our home market, combined with the reach and connectivity of our international network, gives us a strong platform for growth,” Ms Al Rostamani said.

First Abu Dhabi Bank acquires Bahrain's Yasira platform to boost securities services
sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB) announced it has fully acquired Bahrain's Yasira, a financial services platform specializing in fund administration and custody, in a strategic step aimed at strengthening the bank's ability to deliver integrated... solutions.

The acquisition will combine Yasira's fund administration expertise with FAB's leading regional custody capabilities, strengthening the bank's ability to give asset managers and institutional investors integrated solutions spanning public and private markets in the region and beyond.
The Yasira platform supports a wide range of investment strategies, including public assets, private equity, venture capital and real estate, across multiple entities, structures and jurisdictions.
The platform supports private funds throughout their life cycle, from investor commitments to capital calls, distributions and final financial reporting.

The deal will allow FAB to expand its existing custody services and offer more comprehensive solutions to investment managers regionally and internationally, with a particular focus on meeting the growing and complex needs of the Middle East's fund industry.

ADNOC Distribution profit surges 37% on record fuel volumes
sum: Net profit hits Dh2.90b as record fuel volumes and 71 new stations drive 9-month growth
Abu Dhabi: ADNOC Distribution’s net profit rose 37 per cent year on year to $791 million or Dh2.90 billion in the first nine months of 2026, the Abu Dhabi-listed fuel retailer reported on November 9.

EBITDA climbed 26 per cent to Dh4.10 billion or $1.12 billion. Underlying EBITDA grew 14 per cent to Dh3.47 billion or $944 million. Gross profit increased 20 per cent to Dh6.12 billion or $1.67 billion .
Fuel volumes reached a record 11.86 billion litres, including 8.26 billion litres through retail. Non-fuel retail (NFR) gross profit rose 13 per cent to $217 million or Dh797 million.
The board also approved a third-quarter dividend of 5.14 fils per share, worth $175 million or worth Dh643 million. Full-year 2026 dividends are expected to exceed $700 million.

Chief Executive Officer at ADNOC Distribution, Engineer Bader Saeed Al Lamki says the results show the company’s push into higher-margin businesses. “We are building on this momentum to future-proof our growth by scaling higher-margin NFR opportunities and progressing our international strategy,” he said.

He pointed out how its foray into South Affrica is being viewed as a change in the company’s identity. The group is “transforming into a leading international mobility and convenience retailer,” Al Lamki added.

Modon Closes USD 3.7B Syndicated Loan to Fund Development Pipeline
sum: Abu Dhabi-based real estate company Modon Holding secured USD 3.7 billion in financing. Thus, strengthening its liquidity position and extending its debt maturity as it advances its development pipeline.
The AED 13.7 billion facility combines a five-year term loan and a three-year revolving credit line. This is with an additional AED 4 billion accordion option.

The financing gives Modon greater financial flexibility to support its expansion plans without relying solely on new borrowing. By refinancing existing facilities and securing additional funding capacity, the company can manage its debt obligations over a longer period while maintaining resources for upcoming developments.

For investors and businesses operating in Abu Dhabi’s real estate and infrastructure sectors, the transaction also highlights the financing capacity available to large-scale developers as they pursue growth opportunities.
The facility is particularly significant for Modon because it represents the largest financing transaction in the company’s history.

The AED 13.7 billion (USD 3.7 billion) syndicated facility is structured across two tranches. It includes a AED 4.7 billion five-year term loan and a AED 9 billion revolving credit facility with an initial three-year maturity, which can be extended to five years.
The agreement also includes an additional AED 4 billion accordion option, allowing for potential expansion of the facility.

Over 10,000 athletes from 130 countries set to compete at 18th Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship
sum: Abu Dhabi, November 5: The UAE Jiu-Jitsu and Mixed Martial Arts Federation announced the completion of preparations for the 18th Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship during a press conference held at Emirates Palace in Abu Dhabi.

The championship will take place at Mubadala Arena, Zayed Sports City, from November 9 to 21, with more than 10,000 athletes from 130 countries set to compete across various age groups and divisions for a total prize pool of more than AED 3 million. More than 5,000 athletes are expected to travel from outside the UAE to take part.

Mohammed Bin Dalmouj Al Dhaheri, Board Member of the Federation; Mohammed Hussain Al Marzooqi, Board Member of the Federation and Vice Chairman of the Organising Committee; Fahad Ali Al Shamsi, Secretary-General of the Federation; Nasser Khamis Al Marri, Director of the Olympic Sports Department at Abu Dhabi Sports Council; Lieutenant Colonel Dr. Engineer Khalid Ahmed Al Zafin Al Muhairi, Head of the Traffic Engineering and Road Safety Department at Abu Dhabi Police; Yaqoub Al Saadi, Head of Abu Dhabi Sports Channels; Fouad Darwish, CEO and Managing Director of Palms Sports; Saed Hijazi Salameh, General Manager of Sales at Premier Motors; Fahad Al Shaer, Head of Islamic Banking at First Abu Dhabi Bank; and Dr. Hamda Al Neyadi, Director of Marketing and Corporate Communications at PureHealth.

Abu Dhabi World Pro Jiu-Jitsu Championship Ready for More Than 10,000 Athletes
sum: ABU DHABI, UAE — Preparations are complete for the 18th Abu Dhabi World Professional Jiu-Jitsu Championship, with organizers expecting more than 10,000 athletes from 130 countries at Mubadala Arena in Zayed Sports City from November 9 to 21, 2026.

The UAE Jiu-Jitsu and Mixed Martial Arts Federation outlined its final preparations at an Emirates Palace press conference, according to its November 5 announcement. The championship will offer a prize pool exceeding AED 3 million, with more than 5,000 competitors expected to travel from outside the UAE.

The briefing brought together federation officials, government and event partners, former champions and active athletes. Organizers detailed coordination across logistics, security, healthcare and media services ahead of the 13-day competition.
Mohamed Salem Al Dhaheri, the federation’s vice chairman and chairman of the championship organizing committee, said the event reflects years of investment in athletes and the sport.

“The championship’s international success shows the results of the UAE’s long-term investment in sport and athletes, thanks to the continued support of our wise leadership. Over the past 18 years, the championship has become one of the major events on the international jiu-jitsu calendar, bringing together some of the best athletes, clubs and academies from around the world.

“The championship has achieved a lot over the years, and we have a responsibility to keep improving it. We always aim to raise the competition standards and provide a special experience for everyone taking part. Every year, we build on what we have learned from previous editions and work to meet the expectations of the international jiu-jitsu community, while while further reinforcing Abu Dhabi’s position as a global centre for the sport.”
Al Dhaheri said international entrants account for 54 percent of participants, compared with 46 percent from within the UAE.

UAE domestic stocks jump, led by real estate and banks
sum: Dubai, UAE – The Dubai Financial Market index rose by about 1.8% to the level of 5,932.67 points in early trading, Wednesday. Meanwhile, the Abu Dhabi Securities Market index rose 0.95% to 9,553.41 points.

The gains were supported by strong jumps in real estate and banking stocks, especially Emaar shares. Following Emaar Properties’ announcement of its intention to submit an offer to acquire all of the shares it does not own in Emaar Development.
In the Dubai market, Emaar Properties» shares rose 4% to AED 12.24, and Emaar Development shares rose 5% to AED 14.6.

The company explained in a statement on the Dubai Financial Market that the offer amounts to 15 dirhams in cash per share. It is subject to the required approval from the Emaar Properties Board of Directors.
Emaar Properties’ ownership in Emaar Development currently stands at 79.16%. While all shareholders own the remaining 20.84%.
The number of Emaar Development shares is 4 billion shares. The 20.84% to be acquired constitutes approximately 833.6 million shares.
According to the aforementioned price (15 dirhams per share), the total value of the shares to be acquired amounts to approximately 12.5 billion dirhams.

Coal India's arm files IPO papers with Sebi; promoter to offload shares
sum: The proposed IPO is entirely an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 66.81 crore equity shares by its promoter Coal India with no fresh issue component, according to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) dated November 1.
Since the issue is entirely an OFS, SECL will not receive any proceeds from the offering, with the entire proceeds going to Coal India.
Incorporated in 1985 and headquartered in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, SECL is among India's largest coal producers.
It produced 176.29 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for 16.94 per cent of the country's total coal production, DRHP said citing a Crisil report.
SECL's coal production increased 5.25 per cent to 176.29 million tonnes in FY26 from 167.49 million tonnes in the preceding fiscal.
The company was accorded Miniratna Category-I status in March 2007 and completed 40 years of coal mining operations in 2025.
As of April 1, 2026, SECL had total coal geological resources of about 47.55 billion tonnes, accounting for around 11.50 per cent of India's total coal geological resources.
